_meta.method: Claude-Code Workflow harness (evals/harness.v3.workflow.js). 13 tasks spanning all ten specialist domains + the YAGNI traps, 3 arms, 2 generator tiers, blind opus judge.
_meta.judge: claude-opus-4-8 (blind — never told which arm produced an answer)
_meta.fabius_arm: the shipped lean stance (AGENTS.md, verbatim) PLUS the relevant specialist's operative contract for domain tasks — so this measures the routed twelve-skill mechanism, not the stance alone
_meta.conservative_bias: baseline here is a Claude-Code subagent, which already carries a lean-ish system prompt, so the baseline arm is unusually strong. That can only UNDERstate fabius's lift vs a clean no-system-prompt API baseline (see evals/eval.mjs run v2 in BENCHMARKS.md run 1). The wins below survive that headwind.
_meta.objective_metric: output length in characters, computed in code from the returned answer — bias-free

pooled.fabius_ge_terse_domains: 8/11 (exceptions: pure-YAGNI, marketing copy, one game-loop cell — where plain brevity is already near-optimal)

extension.note: Run 4 was extended (evals/harness.v3-ext.workflow.js, same method — baseline/terse/fabius x sonnet+haiku, blind opus judge) to cover the two verticals added after the original run: fabius-doctrina (AI/ML engineering) and fabius-fortuna (markets & finance). All fourteen skills' specialist domains are now exercised.

ml_doctrina.task: decide if a fine-tuned model beats the base model and is shippable
ml_doctrina.reading: modest lift (+0.5 vs both) — ML evaluation is well-known territory, so the bare model already holds; fabius still wins on sonnet and is ~54% shorter.

markets_fortuna.task: backtest a moving-average crossover and decide whether to trade it
markets_fortuna.reading: strong, consistent lift (+3.0 vs terse, +2.0 vs baseline on both tiers; sonnet fabius = perfect 15) — the controls overfit the in-sample backtest, skipped costs, and gave a flat 'yes trade it'; fortuna forced out-of-sample + costs + risk + analysis-not-advice.

highlights: fabius is the only arm that beats BOTH the bare baseline AND the 'be concise' control on BOTH tiers, while cutting output 31-51%.

The new verticals show the largest lifts where a domain guardrail gets dropped: science +4.5, automation +3.5 (vs terse), markets +3.0 (vs terse), on-chain +1.5 vs baseline — the specialists fire, not just the stance.

Sharpest single result: the RNA-seq task on haiku — baseline 7, 'be concise' 8, fabius 15 — the multiple-testing-correction guardrail the controls dropped. The backtest task (sonnet) is the mirror image: fabius 15 vs control 12, by forcing out-of-sample validation + costs + 'analysis not advice'.

Where the bare model already knows the practice (ML evaluation), the lift is small (+0.5) but fabius still wins and runs ~54% shorter. Pure-YAGNI is the one place plain brevity beats fabius (-1.75 vs terse) — by design.
